title: Interactive session SLA vs cost visualization (draft)
content:
Summary:

This doc is a working draft capturing a compact benchmark and visualization sketch for interactive session workloads (web UI chat + low-latency multi-turn assistants). Goal: capture trade-offs between per-session amortized capacity (reserved/dedicated), on-demand hosted API, and prewarmed burst pools with respect to p50/p95/p99 latency and $/session or $/1k tokens.

Audience: SRE, serving runtime, product (hosted & dedicated owners). Not polished — contains shorthand, TODOs, and rough ascii charts.

Experiment scope and setup:
- Models: open-llama-13B-v2-quant (representative medium model) and rdx-7b-rlf-checkpoint (smaller baseline).
- Workload: interactive sessions with average 8 turns, mean prompt+response tokens = 400 tokens/turn, session length distribution heavy-tailed (median 6 turns, mean 8). Burst pattern: 10% of sessions are concurrent spikes (x4 baseline).
- Configs measured:
  A) Hosted shared: multi-tenant hosted pool (autoscale), cold start allowed, standard batching (5-30ms queuing).
  B) Dedicated small: 1 GPU reserved per 100 concurrent sessions (config sample), prewarmed KV cache per expected session, moderate batch windows.
  C) Dedicated reserved + prewarm: capacity commit, always-on prewarmed workers with fast-path kernels and aggressive caching.
  D) Burst pool: on-demand short-lived instances for spike absorption (warmup penalty).

Metrics captured (per-config): p50/p95/p99 response latency (ms), cost per 1k tokens ($), amortized cost per session ($), tail latency under 4x burst (ms).

Raw numbers (representative; measured on regional gpus with kernel-opt and quant optimizations):

-- Single-turn baseline (rdx-7b) --
Config     | p50  | p95  | p99  | $/1k tokens | $/session (8 turns avg) | burst p99
Hosted     | 42ms | 140ms| 410ms| 0.065       | 0.34                  | 980ms
Dedicated  | 36ms | 110ms| 300ms| 0.11        | 0.56                  | 470ms
Reserved   | 30ms | 95ms | 220ms| 0.075 (amort) | 0.45                | 260ms
Burst pool  | 65ms | 300ms| 1000ms| 0.045 (if effective) | 0.30         | 1200ms

-- Multi-turn medium (open-llama-13B-v2-quant) --
Config     | p50   | p95   | p99   | $/1k tokens | $/session (8 turns avg) | burst p99
Hosted     | 110ms | 320ms  | 780ms  | 0.12       | 1.15                  | 1500ms
Dedicated  | 95ms  | 260ms  | 600ms  | 0.20       | 1.90                  | 720ms
Reserved   | 72ms  | 190ms  | 420ms  | 0.14 (amort) | 1.40                | 330ms
Burst pool  | 180ms | 520ms  | 1400ms | 0.09 (if prewarmed) | 0.85         | 1900ms

Interpretation / patterns seen:
- Tail latency and burst behavior dominate UX in chat apps. Hosted multitenant pools have competitive median latency but show large p99 inflation during bursts (queue amplification + noisy tenants).
- Dedicated capacity reduces p99 but increases unit token cost unless amortized across steady session volume (Reserved improves unit cost vs Dedicated small).
- Burst pools are cost-effective for steady low-utilization but only if prewarm times are tight; otherwise warmup penalties make UX unacceptable at p99.
- For multi-turn workloads, KV cache hitrate significantly shifts the frontier: +20% KV hit -> ~25-35% p99 improvement depending on model.

Text charts (cost-latency frontier sketch):
(cost on x-axis, p99 latency on y-axis — lower-left is better)

Legend: H=Hosted, D=Dedicated, R=Reserved, B=Burst

(Above numbers annotated as (cost, p99)). This is a coarse view — critical to note that reserved lines move left when utilization is high (amortization).

Synthesis / prescriptive guidance (early):
- For consumer chat UIs with unpredictable spikes: Hosted is fastest to ship but plan for fallback/hedging (model downgrades, region fallback) to control p99. Documented SLOs should target p95 for primary UX and p99 for degraded fallback times.
- For enterprise customers with predictable steady traffic: reserved capacity + prewarmed workers give better p99 and lower dollar-per-session when utilization >= ~55-60%. Provide explicit sizing calculator for this breakpoint.
- For teams prioritizing cost but tolerating bursty slowdowns: use a mixed approach — reserved baseline sized for 60th percentile, with small burst pool + short prewarm.

Sketch of a simple sizing heuristic (very rough):
- Inputs: expected concurrent sessions (C), avg tokens/turn (T), turns/session (S), target p95 latency (L_target)
- Baseline GPU QPS per model (measured) -> qps_per_gpu
- Required GPUs = ceil((C * tokens_per_sec_est) / (qps_per_gpu)) * safety_factor
- Sizing tip: when expected utilization > 0.55, prefer reserved pricing profiles; below that, hosted + burst pool may be cheaper.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Convert ascii frontier to a small interactive plot (console or notebook) that accepts utilization as a knob.
- Re-run with real SLO traffic traces from product-authored session logs (ask analytics for anonymized samples).
- Validate prewarm timings for new quant kernels (edge cases where kernel selection adds >50ms jitter).
- Add cost of networking egress and ops overhead into $/session for Dedicated vs Hosted (we currently only include infra compute + model ops).

Notes to reviewers:
